name: Fashion bible
about: Menswear rules, tips and example outfits, in the Smart Wardrobe app's vocabulary (garment types, colours, styles, fits and occasions as in app.js). Score an outfit with: sigmoid(model.bias + sum(rule.weight * check(rule))).

rules.title: Neutrals first, one accent colour
rules.why: Navy, grey, white, beige, brown, olive and black all go together; one brighter colour on top of them looks chosen, two or three look random.

rules.title: Three colours at most
rules.why: Past three colours an outfit gets busy and the eye has nowhere to rest.

rules.title: Mix light and dark
rules.why: Contrast between top and bottom gives the outfit shape; all mid-tones look flat.

rules.title: Tonal dressing works
rules.why: Shades of one colour from head to toe look calm and expensive.

rules.title: Classic colour pairings
rules.why: Some top and bottom colours are proven together: navy and grey, white and denim, olive and cream.

rules.title: Colours that fight
rules.why: Two loud colours of similar strength compete instead of working together.

rules.title: Keep pieces at one level of dressiness
rules.why: A very casual piece next to a very dressy one makes both look wrong; step at most one level apart.

rules.title: Dress for the occasion
rules.why: Being clearly under- or overdressed is the most noticed mistake; aim for the level of the room.

rules.title: Styles that suit the occasion
rules.why: Each occasion has its own vocabulary: tailoring for work, sportswear for the gym.

rules.title: Don't mix gym kit with tailoring
rules.why: Sportswear and formal pieces come from different worlds; together they look accidental.

rules.title: One story per outfit
rules.why: When every piece shares a style the outfit reads as intentional.

rules.title: Balance volume
rules.why: A roomy top looks best over slimmer trousers and the other way round; roomy on roomy only works as a deliberate streetwear look.

rules.title: One statement piece
rules.why: A big graphic, logo or loud piece needs quiet pieces around it to stand out.

rules.title: Go easy on patterns
rules.why: One pattern is easy. Two need clearly different scales (fine stripe with a large check), so most days keep it to one.

rules.title: Denim on denim needs contrast
rules.why: A denim top with jeans in the same wash reads as a uniform; pick clearly different washes or break it up.

rules.title: Shoes at the level of the outfit
rules.why: Shoes are read first: dress shoes with joggers or trainers with a tie break the look.

rules.title: Belt matches the shoes
rules.why: With leather shoes, the belt is in the same colour family: black with black, brown with brown.

rules.title: A tie needs a collar and long trousers
rules.why: A tie only works with a collared shirt and tailored trousers, never with a hoodie or shorts.

rules.title: Suits want shirts and leather shoes
rules.why: A suit is the dressiest thing most men own; a T-shirt or trainers pull it down to casual.

rules.title: The coat matches the outfit
rules.why: A puffer or rain shell over tailoring undoes it; an overcoat finishes a smart outfit.

rules.title: One metal for accessories
rules.why: Watch, rings and bracelet look tidier all gold or all silver.

rules.title: Dress for the temperature
rules.why: Too many layers is as uncomfortable as too few: about one warm layer above 24°C, three or four when mild, six or more when cold.

rules.title: Shorts only when it's warm
rules.why: Shorts below about 17°C look out of season.

rules.title: Ready for rain
rules.why: On wet days a jacket that sheds water and shoes that don't mind puddles; suede and white trainers suffer.

rules.title: Fabrics for the season
rules.why: Linen and seersucker for heat, tweed, flannel and corduroy for cold.

rules.title: Sports clothes for training
rules.why: At the gym, clothes made to move and breathe, and proper training shoes.

tips.why: They are far too casual for the occasion.
sources: What to Wear as a Wedding Guest

tips.text: A tuxedo should be black or midnight blue, not a brighter blue.
tips.why: Other colours break the black-tie code.
sources: What to Wear as a Wedding Guest

tips.text: Avoid white clothing that could compete with the bride.
tips.why: White is traditionally reserved for her.
sources: What to Wear as a Wedding Guest

tips.text: Choose solid-coloured shoes over multicoloured ones when you want to look smart.
tips.why: A single colour reads cleaner and more formal.
sources: How To Match Clothes and Shoes For Guys: Outfit Color Guide

tips.text: Darker shoes are dressier and more versatile than lighter ones.
tips.why: Dark leather pairs with more outfits and formal settings.
sources: How To Match Clothes and Shoes For Guys: Outfit Color Guide

tips.text: Wear black shoes with black suits and tuxedos, and with grey or charcoal suits in formal offices.
tips.why: Black is the most formal shoe colour.
sources: How To Match Clothes and Shoes For Guys: Outfit Color Guide

tips.text: Brown shoes suit almost everything except black suits and the most formal offices.
tips.why: Brown is less formal than black but far more versatile.
sources: How To Match Clothes and Shoes For Guys: Outfit Color Guide

tips.text: Printed twill or jacquard silk ties are dressier than knitted ties.
tips.why: Knit ties have a more casual texture.
sources: How To Dress Like An Italian

tips.text: Keep polished oxfords for the occasions and jobs that still call for them.
tips.why: Sneakers don't replace formal shoes everywhere.
sources: How To Wear Sneakers With Tailoring

tips.text: Read care labels first: most clothes can be washed at home, but tailored jackets and suits usually need dry cleaning.
tips.why: Washing tailoring can ruin its structure.
sources: The Intelligent Man's Guide To Wardrobe Maintenance

tips.text: Sort laundry into whites, colours and delicates, and wash each load separately.
tips.why: Mixing them leads to dye transfer and damaged delicate fabrics.
sources: The Intelligent Man's Guide To Wardrobe Maintenance

tips.text: Wash new dark or indigo pieces on their own for the first few washes.
tips.why: Fresh dyes bleed onto other clothes.
sources: The Intelligent Man's Guide To Wardrobe Maintenance

tips.text: Avoid the tumble dryer.
tips.why: Its heat shrinks and wears out clothes.
sources: The Intelligent Man's Guide To Wardrobe Maintenance

tips.text: Hang tailored jackets and overcoats on broad, correctly sized hangers, never wire hangers or coat pegs.
tips.why: Poor support distorts the shoulders.
sources: The Intelligent Man's Guide To Wardrobe Maintenance

tips.text: Clean tailoring before storing it for long, and keep it in breathable, moth-proof garment bags.
tips.why: Moths go for dirty wool, and plastic traps moisture.
sources: The Intelligent Man's Guide To Wardrobe Maintenance

tips.text: Check the jacket's back: apart from slight folds under the arms it should be smooth, free of horizontal or vertical wrinkles.
tips.why: A clean back is the best overall sign that the jacket fits.
sources: How A Suit Should Fit

tips.text: Buttoned, the front should form a clean V above and fall slightly open below; X-shaped pulls mean too tight, vertical folds too loose.
tips.why: These creases reveal fit at a glance.
sources: How A Suit Should Fit

tips.text: Suit trousers should be neither tight nor baggy, with pleats lying flat and a slight break or none.
tips.why: Clean trouser lines finish the suit.
sources: How A Suit Should Fit

tips.text: When between sizes, take the larger one.
tips.why: Taking a garment in is much easier than letting it out.
sources: A Basic Guide On Alterations

tips.text: Wear the shoes and layers you'll pair with a garment to fittings: dress shoes and shirt for a suit, a sweater under a coat.
tips.why: Lengths and ease are set against what you'll actually wear.
sources: A Basic Guide On Alterations

tips.text: Lapels should lie flat against the chest without gaping or lifting.
tips.why: Gaping lapels make even a costly suit look cheap.
sources: How Should a Suit Fit

tips.text: The jacket should button without pulling, leaving room to slide a flat hand inside.
tips.why: Too tight causes strain lines; too loose looks sloppy.
sources: How Should a Suit Fit

tips.text: Read the jacket's back: horizontal creases mean too tight, vertical folds mean excess cloth, and spreading vents mean tight hips or seat.
tips.why: The back exposes fit problems that are hard to hide.
sources: How Should a Suit Fit

tips.text: Choose the size that fits shoulders, chest and seat, then have the waist, sleeves and trouser length tailored.
tips.why: Structural changes are costly and rarely succeed, and making a suit smaller is easier than larger.
sources: How Should a Suit Fit

tips.text: Don't wear a suit jacket with jeans; smooth, structured suiting clashes with denim.
tips.why: A formal jacket over casual jeans looks like an orphaned suit piece.
sources: How To Wear A Blazer And Jeans Without Looking Like Your Dad

tips.text: Keep proportions together: a wide tie, a bulky knot and a spread collar go as a set, as do a slim tie, a small knot and a standard collar.
tips.why: Mismatched sizes make the knot look lost or crammed.
sources: A Tie Guide: Everything You Need to Know Before Putting One On

tips.text: With a dark suit at a cocktail-dress event, wear dark socks with your loafers.
tips.why: Bare ankles are too casual for that level of formality.
sources: Should You Wear Socks With Loafers?

tips.text: Don't make classic clothes look too perfect or bought together; a slightly careless, accumulated look reads more stylish.
tips.why: Clothes that look lived in seem effortless.
sources: The 3 Ralph Lauren Aesthetics Every Man Can Wear This Fall
Alain Delon Style Breakdown | Why Everything Worked
A Man's Guide to '90s Minimalism

tips.text: Dress for the job and life you are aiming for, not the one you had at school; clothes signal whether people can trust you with responsibility.
tips.why: People judge competence partly by appearance.
sources: TOM FORD | Project Upgrade | Full Version

tips.text: Wearing one rich dark colour such as brown head to toe can feel heavy; add a white or light piece to lift it.
tips.why: A light element breaks up a dense block of colour.
sources: TOM FORD | Project Upgrade | Full Version

tips.text: Jeans should not be so short that they leave a gap above the shoe, and laced shoes should be laced properly.
tips.why: Small details make an outfit look careless.
sources: TOM FORD | Project Upgrade | Full Version

tips.text: Choose pieces that get better with age: a suede jacket, a slightly rumpled linen shirt, an olive field jacket, brown loafers that have been walked in.
tips.why: Clothes that acquire character look personal.
sources: When the Mall Taught Men How to Dress: J.Crew, Banana Republic & Gap

tips.text: When buying vintage or second-hand, check the garment's measurements rather than the size on the label, and favour natural fabrics.
tips.why: Sizing changes over the years; natural fibres last.
sources: When the Mall Taught Men How to Dress: J.Crew, Banana Republic & Gap

tips.text: A crisp white shirt gives the strongest contrast with a dark suit.
tips.why: High contrast looks sharp and clean.
sources: How to Dress Like Tom Ford

tips.text: French cuffs with cufflinks are one of the few pieces of jewellery a classic dresser can wear.
tips.why: They add detail without looking flashy.
sources: How to Dress Like Tom Ford

tips.text: Leaving a shirt open three buttons deep is a fashion-world look; in normal settings one or two open buttons is enough.
tips.why: Too much chest looks out of place at work.
sources: How to Dress Like Tom Ford

tips.text: Tie the tie with a dimple under the knot; a black knit or silk tie keeps a monochrome outfit coherent.
tips.why: A dimple looks finished.
sources: How to Dress Like Tom Ford

tips.text: A good watch should be discovered rather than announced, and should suit the rest of the outfit.
tips.why: Understated luxury looks more confident.
sources: How to Dress Like Tom Ford

tips.text: For a rugged casual look, pair slim dark jeans and brown leather boots with a denim shirt and a suede trucker jacket.
tips.why: Rugged textures and earth tones dress down well.
sources: How to Dress Like Tom Ford

tips.text: Wear preppy clothes like a grown man who left university years ago: skip novelty varsity sweatshirts and build on an oxford, knitwear, chinos and a tweed jacket.
tips.why: Adult prep looks refined; student prep looks like a costume.
sources: The 3 Ralph Lauren Aesthetics Every Man Can Wear This Fall

tips.text: For autumn knitwear, collect cream, oatmeal, burgundy, forest green and navy; they all combine with khaki, olive and stone chinos.
tips.why: A coherent palette makes everything mix.
sources: The 3 Ralph Lauren Aesthetics Every Man Can Wear This Fall

tips.text: Grey flannel trousers are the step up from chinos when an autumn outfit needs to be dressier.
tips.why: Flannel is smart but soft and textured.
sources: The 3 Ralph Lauren Aesthetics Every Man Can Wear This Fall

tips.text: Autumn lets you layer patterns: a striped oxford under a Fair Isle sweater, a tartan scarf over a camel coat, a striped tie under a cardigan.
tips.why: Heavier textures make pattern mixing look natural.
sources: The 3 Ralph Lauren Aesthetics Every Man Can Wear This Fall

tips.text: Shop for specific ingredients, such as a brown herringbone sport coat or a navy lambswool crew neck, rather than a brand or logo; second-hand is fine.
tips.why: The look comes from the pieces, not the label.
sources: The 3 Ralph Lauren Aesthetics Every Man Can Wear This Fall

tips.text: In cold months, texture matters most: swap light chinos for olive or tobacco corduroy and bring in tweed, flannel, suede, waxed cotton and Shetland wool.
tips.why: Rich textures make simple outfits interesting.
sources: The 3 Ralph Lauren Aesthetics Every Man Can Wear This Fall

tips.text: Country-style outerwear such as a waxed field jacket, quilted jacket, barn coat or brown wool overcoat pairs with grounded shoes: suede chukkas, country derbies or leather boots.
tips.why: Rugged pieces need sturdy footwear.
sources: The 3 Ralph Lauren Aesthetics Every Man Can Wear This Fall

tips.text: For a Western touch, take one or two rugged elements and set them in normal clothes; never wear every cowboy signifier at once.
tips.why: One accent reads as style, the full set as fancy dress.
sources: The 3 Ralph Lauren Aesthetics Every Man Can Wear This Fall

tips.text: Rugged outerwear options: a suede trucker, a shearling-lined coat, a worn leather bomber or a denim ranch jacket.
tips.why: Outerwear carries this look the most.
sources: The 3 Ralph Lauren Aesthetics Every Man Can Wear This Fall

tips.text: Old leather and suede jackets bought second-hand already have the patina brands charge extra to fake.
tips.why: Wear adds character for free.
sources: The 3 Ralph Lauren Aesthetics Every Man Can Wear This Fall

tips.text: Start with silhouette: high-waisted trousers with a crease and a jacket with a defined shoulder give tailoring a strong frame.
tips.why: Proportion is the foundation of good tailoring.
sources: A TAKE ON MODERN TAILORING | In Conversation with Mike Amiri & GQ Italia

tips.text: When mixing a bold patterned shirt with tailoring, choose muted colours that blend with the suit rather than loud ones.
tips.why: Toned-down patterns stay believable and wearable.
sources: A TAKE ON MODERN TAILORING | In Conversation with Mike Amiri & GQ Italia

tips.text: Pointed boots under creased trousers extend the line of the leg; with a higher waist they make legs look longer.
tips.why: An unbroken vertical line adds height.
sources: A TAKE ON MODERN TAILORING | In Conversation with Mike Amiri & GQ Italia

tips.text: Clothes should amplify your personality, not wear you; one personal touch such as a belt buckle, a pin, necklaces or a vintage watch makes tailoring yours.
tips.why: Wearing something comfortably is what makes it look good.
sources: A TAKE ON MODERN TAILORING | In Conversation with Mike Amiri & GQ Italia

tips.text: For hot weather, choose half-canvas, light jackets with a light silk or open shirt so a suit can go from lunch to dinner.
tips.why: Light construction keeps tailoring wearable in heat.
sources: A TAKE ON MODERN TAILORING | In Conversation with Mike Amiri & GQ Italia

tips.text: When building a wardrobe from scratch, balance categories: a few bottoms, a few tops, a layer and one pair of shoes, rather than many of one thing.
tips.why: A balanced set makes more outfits.
sources: Rebuilding My Wardrobe with ONLY Cotton On...

tips.text: Skip colours you already own several of; add pieces that expand your rotation instead.
tips.why: Duplicates add little new outfit potential.
sources: Rebuilding My Wardrobe with ONLY Cotton On...

tips.text: A matching sweatsuit only works when top and bottom are truly the same shade; near-misses look accidental.
tips.why: Slightly different tones of one colour clash.
sources: Rebuilding My Wardrobe with ONLY Cotton On...

tips.text: Plain socks without visible logos look tidier with clogs and sandals.
tips.why: Branded socks distract.
sources: Rebuilding My Wardrobe with ONLY Cotton On...

tips.text: Baggy bootcut jeans pair naturally with boots; their flare sits over the shoe.
tips.why: The cut was made for boots.
sources: Rebuilding My Wardrobe with ONLY Cotton On...

tips.text: Think about colour before buying a layer: a brown zip-up goes with darker or bootcut jeans and a white tee more easily than with a busy graphic.
tips.why: Check new pieces against what you will wear them with.
sources: Rebuilding My Wardrobe with ONLY Cotton On...

tips.text: Aim to look exceptionally well dressed while seeming barely to have tried: precise, understated clothes with no unnecessary details.
tips.why: Restraint reads as confidence.
sources: James Bond Style Explained | How to Dress Like 007

tips.text: Choose clothes for your own build rather than copying a celebrity's exact cut; slimmer, broader or shorter men need different proportions.
tips.why: The goal is the effect, not someone else's measurements.
sources: James Bond Style Explained | How to Dress Like 007

tips.text: A Harrington, simple bomber or lightweight blouson over a polo and jeans makes a timeless urban casual look; the silhouette matters more than the label.
tips.why: Clean short jackets suit everyday wear.
sources: James Bond Style Explained | How to Dress Like 007

tips.text: A clean polo, chinos and loafers or suede shoes is the ideal middle ground between sloppy and formal.
tips.why: Casual clothes held to formal standards of fit.
sources: James Bond Style Explained | How to Dress Like 007

tips.text: Suede chukkas bridge rugged and refined: smarter than sneakers, less formal than dress shoes, and they go with almost any trousers.
tips.why: Versatile shoes cover more outfits.
sources: James Bond Style Explained | How to Dress Like 007

tips.text: A few versatile shoes cover most needs: dark chukkas, dark leather boots, clean minimal sneakers and a pair of loafers.
tips.why: Shoes that cross categories save money.
sources: James Bond Style Explained | How to Dress Like 007

tips.text: Don't wear every piece associated with a style icon at once; the result looks like cosplay.
tips.why: Subtle inspiration looks stylish; a full copy looks like a costume.
sources: James Bond Style Explained | How to Dress Like 007

tips.text: Know your measurements and what fits your body; a lean frame of average height looks best between tailored and relaxed, not skin tight.
tips.why: Clothes with shape and some ease look natural rather than tense.
sources: Alain Delon Style Breakdown | Why Everything Worked

tips.text: Smooth cotton shirts look sharper and keep the collar in shape; linen shirts look relaxed and sunny.
tips.why: The fabric sets the mood of the outfit.
sources: Alain Delon Style Breakdown | Why Everything Worked

tips.text: When dressing formally, do it properly: a well-tailored oxford, quiet colours and everything buttoned as it should be.
tips.why: There is a time and place for relaxed details.
sources: Alain Delon Style Breakdown | Why Everything Worked

tips.text: Own trousers in several fabrics, such as cotton twill, linen, chinos and denim, mostly in neutral colours; the same few shapes look different each time.
tips.why: Material variety multiplies outfits.
sources: Alain Delon Style Breakdown | Why Everything Worked

tips.text: Use contrast between shirt and trousers: a dark shirt with light trousers or a white shirt with dark trousers.
tips.why: Contrast gives an outfit definition.
sources: Alain Delon Style Breakdown | Why Everything Worked

tips.text: Jackets should be structured but not stiff, with clean shoulders and a length that frames the body; not so long it swallows you, not cropped for fashion's sake.
tips.why: A balanced jacket supports the outfit instead of dominating it.
sources: Alain Delon Style Breakdown | Why Everything Worked

tips.text: Pick knitwear colours that contrast with the shirts you own: dark charcoal, black or grey knits over white and light blue shirts.
tips.why: Without contrast the outfit looks dull.
sources: Alain Delon Style Breakdown | Why Everything Worked

tips.text: Choose suit cloth with enough weight to drape; in summer, wear lighter linen and cotton suits in pale colours.
tips.why: The right fabric keeps a suit from looking flat or cheap.
sources: Alain Delon Style Breakdown | Why Everything Worked

tips.text: Keep belts simple: plain black or brown leather with an understated buckle.
tips.why: A belt should hold the outfit together, not distract.
sources: Alain Delon Style Breakdown | Why Everything Worked

tips.text: Loafers suit a relaxed Riviera style; espadrilles or moccasins can be worn without socks in summer.
tips.why: Soft slip-ons fit warm-weather tailoring.
sources: Alain Delon Style Breakdown | Why Everything Worked

tips.text: If your feet get wider, pick sneaker models or low-tops that fit wide, or go up a size, rather than squeezing into your old size.
tips.why: Shoes that fit are worn more and look better.
sources: Cody Rhodes Goes Sneaker Shopping With Complex

tips.text: Don't pay luxury prices for jackets made of polyurethane or other plastic coatings.
tips.why: The material is cheap and ages badly whatever the label says.
sources: PERCHÉ NON TUTTI I CAPI MADE IN ITALY SONO UGUALI con Mattia Berveglieri | Live Talk @ WHITE Milano

tips.text: For hoodies and sweatshirts, a heavy fleece of around 400 to 500 grams per square metre is a sign of quality.
tips.why: Heavier fabric holds its shape and lasts longer.
sources: PERCHÉ NON TUTTI I CAPI MADE IN ITALY SONO UGUALI con Mattia Berveglieri | Live Talk @ WHITE Milano

tips.text: A plain T-shirt in premium cotton with careful stitching can justify a higher price; a very cheap tee usually cuts corners on fibre, dye or labour.
tips.why: Good fabric and assembly cost money.
sources: PERCHÉ NON TUTTI I CAPI MADE IN ITALY SONO UGUALI con Mattia Berveglieri | Live Talk @ WHITE Milano

tips.text: Before buying a coat sold as wool, check how much wool is really in it; a large share of polyester lowers its warmth and value.
tips.why: Blends are often marketed as wool.
sources: PERCHÉ NON TUTTI I CAPI MADE IN ITALY SONO UGUALI con Mattia Berveglieri | Live Talk @ WHITE Milano

tips.text: If you work behind the scenes or want to blend in, an all-black outfit of simple basics is practical and always looks put together.
tips.why: Black basics are discreet and easy to combine.
sources: What Are People Wearing in Tokyo? (Fashion Trends 2026 Street Style Ep.207)

tips.text: Match fragrance to the season: light, fresh scents such as citrus for hot days, stronger sweet scents for cold weather and evenings.
tips.why: Heavy scents overwhelm in heat; light ones vanish in the cold.
sources: THE LAST Fragrance Guide You Will EVER Need

tips.text: If you own only one fragrance, make it a fresh, not-too-loud one that suits every occasion.
tips.why: Smelling fresh is never wrong; smelling very sweet often is.
sources: THE LAST Fragrance Guide You Will EVER Need

tips.text: Add a sweeter, warmer fragrance as your second, for evenings, dates and winter.
tips.why: Two scents cover day and night.
sources: THE LAST Fragrance Guide You Will EVER Need

tips.text: Don't wear a heavy sweet fragrance to the gym or in close quiet places like a library.
tips.why: Strong scent in the wrong place bothers people around you.
sources: THE LAST Fragrance Guide You Will EVER Need

tips.text: Spray strong scents about three times (sides of the neck and a wrist), lighter fresh scents about five, and adjust to each fragrance.
tips.why: Concentration varies, so dose accordingly.
sources: THE LAST Fragrance Guide You Will EVER Need

tips.text: Use an unscented deodorant so it doesn't clash with your fragrance.
tips.why: Competing scents muddy each other.
sources: THE LAST Fragrance Guide You Will EVER Need

tips.text: EDT, EDP and extrait are concentrations; higher usually lasts longer, but versions with the same name often smell different, so test each.
tips.why: The label doesn't guarantee the same scent.
sources: THE LAST Fragrance Guide You Will EVER Need

tips.text: A waxed cotton or canvas jacket is a buy-for-life piece: hard-wearing, easy to repair and re-waxable when it loses its water resistance.
tips.why: Unlike plastic-coated jackets, it can be renewed and gains patina.
sources: 11 Things You Only Need To Buy Once (they will last forever)

tips.text: Choose Goodyear-welted (or Blake-stitched) leather boots and shoes; they can be resoled instead of thrown away.
tips.why: A glued sole that fails ends the shoe.
sources: 11 Things You Only Need To Buy Once (they will last forever)

tips.text: Good full-grain leather shoes mould to your feet over time and polish back up beautifully.
tips.why: Quality leather gets more comfortable with wear.
sources: 11 Things You Only Need To Buy Once (they will last forever)

tips.text: Merino wool socks are worth paying more for: comfortable, temperature regulating and long-lasting.
tips.why: You wear socks every day.
sources: 11 Things You Only Need To Buy Once (they will last forever)

tips.text: Buy belts in single-piece full-grain leather; 'genuine leather' is often bonded scraps that split.
tips.why: Full-grain leather lasts and ages well.
sources: 11 Things You Only Need To Buy Once (they will last forever)

tips.text: A mechanical watch in a timeless design, such as a field watch, outlasts a smartwatch; swap a fabric strap for steel to dress it up.
tips.why: It keeps working for decades with care.
sources: 11 Things You Only Need To Buy Once (they will last forever)

tips.text: Five shoes cover almost everything: a daily shoe, an active shoe, a dressy shoe, a beater for bad weather and chores, and a comfort shoe.
tips.why: Each role gets covered without buying pairs you never wear.
sources: The Only 5 Shoes Everyone Should Own

tips.text: Your daily shoe must be versatile, durable and comfortable; a retro runner in a clean colourway works with most casual outfits.
tips.why: You wear it more than any other pair.
sources: The Only 5 Shoes Everyone Should Own

tips.text: Have one versatile training shoe for running, gym and general activity rather than many specialist pairs, unless you do one sport seriously.
tips.why: One good hybrid shoe handles most activity.
sources: The Only 5 Shoes Everyone Should Own

tips.text: For dress shoes, ignore trends like chunky or sneaker loafers and buy a timeless shape; plain derbies are the most versatile.
tips.why: Rarely worn shoes should still match your style years later.
sources: The Only 5 Shoes Everyone Should Own

tips.text: Keep a beater pair, such as an old daily shoe or a durable hiking shoe, for rain, mud and chores.
tips.why: It saves your good shoes and lets them last for years.
sources: The Only 5 Shoes Everyone Should Own

tips.text: For a summer suit that wrinkles less than pure linen, choose a linen-silk blend; the jacket and trousers also work as separates.
tips.why: Silk reduces creasing and the pieces can be reworn with jeans or a tee.
sources: Mi faccio creare un abito custom made da Suitsupply per Miami

tips.text: Wool-mohair is a light, crisp suiting with a slight sheen, a good alternative to tropical wool for warm-weather events.
tips.why: Mohair adds lightness and resists creasing.
sources: Mi faccio creare un abito custom made da Suitsupply per Miami

tips.text: Half-lined or unlined jackets are cooler and move more easily; unlined construction needs cleaner internal seams.
tips.why: Less lining means more comfort in heat.
sources: Mi faccio creare un abito custom made da Suitsupply per Miami

tips.text: Prefer canvassed jackets over fused ones; a full canvas keeps its shape for years, while fused jackets lose structure over time.
tips.why: Sewn canvas lets the cloth drape and last.
sources: Mi faccio creare un abito custom made da Suitsupply per Miami

tips.text: Flap pockets suit business suits, jetted pockets are more ceremonial, and patch pockets are the casual choice for blazers.
tips.why: Pocket style sets a jacket's formality.
sources: Mi faccio creare un abito custom made da Suitsupply per Miami

tips.text: Choose shoulder construction to suit your posture and build: padded for structure, soft or Neapolitan for a relaxed look.
tips.why: The shoulder defines the silhouette.
sources: Mi faccio creare un abito custom made da Suitsupply per Miami

tips.text: Trousers worn with a double-breasted jacket look clean with side adjusters instead of belt loops, and a single pleat adds softness.
tips.why: No belt keeps the line uninterrupted.
sources: Mi faccio creare un abito custom made da Suitsupply per Miami

tips.text: For trousers meant to fall softly onto the shoe, skip the turn-up and set the final length after trying them with the shoes you'll wear.
tips.why: Hem length depends on the shoe.
sources: Mi faccio creare un abito custom made da Suitsupply per Miami

tips.text: Have trousers made slightly roomy at the waist and hips; taking them in is easy, letting them out is barely possible.
tips.why: Seam allowance is usually only about a centimetre.
sources: Mi faccio creare un abito custom made da Suitsupply per Miami

tips.text: Dry-clean a suit rarely, about once a season, and warn the cleaner about delicate buttons such as mother-of-pearl.
tips.why: Frequent cleaning wears out the cloth.
sources: Mi faccio creare un abito custom made da Suitsupply per Miami

tips.text: A suit should feel relaxed rather than tight, with no pulling across the back or at the armholes.
tips.why: A suit that strains looks borrowed.
sources: Mi faccio creare un abito custom made da Suitsupply per Miami

tips.text: A higher Super number means a finer, lighter, more delicate wool cloth.
tips.why: Super numbers grade how fine the wool fibre is; finer cloth feels lighter but is less hard-wearing.
sources: Mi faccio creare un abito custom made da Suitsupply per Miami

tips.text: Minimalism is about removing visual noise, not only wearing black: grey, brown, navy, cream, olive or burgundy work as long as pieces don't compete.
tips.why: Silhouette, fabric and the wearer matter more than decoration.
sources: A Man's Guide to '90s Minimalism

tips.text: Choose controlled volume: trousers with room through the hip that taper gently, and relaxed jackets that still follow the body.
tips.why: It sits between 2010s skinny and today's oversized extremes.
sources: A Man's Guide to '90s Minimalism

tips.text: You can look grown-up without a tie: a black crew neck loosely tucked into charcoal wool trousers, or a white tee under a dark blazer.
tips.why: Maturity comes from proportion, restraint and materials.
sources: A Man's Guide to '90s Minimalism

tips.text: Start a minimal wardrobe with trousers that have presence: pleated or flat-front charcoal wool that doesn't cling to thigh or calf.
tips.why: Fuller trousers give simple tops shape.
sources: A Man's Guide to '90s Minimalism

tips.text: Contrast soft and hard materials: wool trousers with leather shoes, knitwear under a leather jacket, a structured leather bag with relaxed clothes.
tips.why: Hard materials stop minimalism looking bland.
sources: A Man's Guide to '90s Minimalism

tips.text: Tight all-black clothes such as skinny black jeans, a tight shirt and a cropped jacket miss the point of minimalism; the clothes need air around the body.
tips.why: Colour alone doesn't make the look; silhouette does.
sources: A Man's Guide to '90s Minimalism

tips.text: Wear black as the main colour with camel as the accent, roughly a 70/30 split, for example an all-black outfit under a camel coat.
tips.why: Striking contrast with very little risk.
sources: 5 Colour Combinations That Always Work

tips.text: If brown feels hard to wear, choose camel instead of dark brown; it is lighter and sits easily with black, white and grey.
tips.why: Lighter browns are more forgiving than dark chocolate shades.
sources: 5 Colour Combinations That Always Work

tips.text: Pick camel pieces in wool or other textured fabrics.
tips.why: Texture adds depth to a plain, light colour.
sources: 5 Colour Combinations That Always Work

tips.text: Pair deep navy with burgundy rather than bright blue with purple.
tips.why: The dark versions look rich and smart; the bright ones look harsh, like a bruise.
sources: 5 Colour Combinations That Always Work

tips.text: Wear a burgundy roll neck under a navy suit, or tucked into pleated trousers, for a smart pairing without a shirt and tie.
tips.why: Navy grounds the look and burgundy adds richness.
sources: 5 Colour Combinations That Always Work

tips.text: Ground dark green trousers with brown shoes such as brogues or derbies.
tips.why: Green and brown are a natural pairing and dark green suits most builds.
sources: 5 Colour Combinations That Always Work

tips.text: Combine pink with soft neutrals, especially grey, rather than with other strong colours.
tips.why: The neutral calms the pink so it doesn't overwhelm the outfit.
sources: 5 Colour Combinations That Always Work

tips.text: Avoid wearing red and green together.
tips.why: The pairing looks like a Christmas costume.
sources: 5 Colour Combinations That Always Work

tips.text: In a black and white outfit, aim for about 70/30: one piece in one colour and the rest in the other, rather than alternating pieces head to toe.
tips.why: Alternating black and white items looks like zebra stripes.
sources: 8 Outfit Colour Matching Combinations That Always Work

tips.text: Try navy with cream for smart casual outfits, such as an unstructured navy blazer with cream chinos.
tips.why: It has the contrast of black and white but feels softer.
sources: 8 Outfit Colour Matching Combinations That Always Work

tips.text: For autumn and winter, wear brown with beige as a tonal pairing, such as brown outerwear over beige trousers.
tips.why: The two shades sit together naturally in the colder months.
sources: 8 Outfit Colour Matching Combinations That Always Work

tips.text: Break up a brown and beige outfit with white, or a touch of muted green or burnt orange.
tips.why: A small contrast stops a tonal look from going flat.
sources: 8 Outfit Colour Matching Combinations That Always Work

tips.text: Pair dark green with black, especially in tailoring, for example a green blazer over a black roll neck for cocktail attire.
tips.why: Two dark colours together look rich and evening-appropriate.
sources: 8 Outfit Colour Matching Combinations That Always Work

tips.text: Use olive with white in summer, dressed up with tailoring or down with a tee and cargo trousers.
tips.why: The pairing is fresh and works at both ends of the formality scale.
sources: 8 Outfit Colour Matching Combinations That Always Work

tips.text: When combining brown and green, add white accents such as white sneakers.
tips.why: Without some white the earthy pairing can look dull and dated.
sources: 8 Outfit Colour Matching Combinations That Always Work

tips.text: For an easy low-risk outfit, mix different shades of grey, starting with dark charcoal against light grey.
tips.why: Greys always sit together; the shade difference keeps it interesting.
sources: 8 Outfit Colour Matching Combinations That Always Work

tips.text: Wear pink with blue in pale or pastel shades for casual spring and summer looks, not in the most saturated tones.
tips.why: Bright versions of the two colours tend to clash.
sources: 8 Outfit Colour Matching Combinations That Always Work

tips.text: When combining different pattern types, choose ones that look clearly different, such as stripes with florals, not dots with puppytooth.
tips.why: Patterns that are too alike blur together and look like a mistake.
sources: An Expert Guide To Pattern Mixing

tips.text: If wearing three patterns, make one small, one medium and one large; a patterned tie or pocket square can be the third.
tips.why: Graduated scales let each pattern read on its own.
sources: An Expert Guide To Pattern Mixing

tips.text: Put the boldest pattern on the outer layer and keep quieter patterns underneath.
tips.why: The loud piece leads and the rest supports it.
sources: An Expert Guide To Pattern Mixing

tips.text: Start pattern mixing with checks.
tips.why: Checks are the easiest pattern for most men to wear.
sources: An Expert Guide To Pattern Mixing

tips.text: When clashing two checks, keep them in a family of related colours.
tips.why: A shared palette lets different-sized checks look deliberate.
sources: An Expert Guide To Pattern Mixing

tips.text: To mix stripes with stripes, vary their width or direction, for example horizontal stripes under vertical ones.
tips.why: A change of width or direction separates the two layers.
sources: An Expert Guide To Pattern Mixing

tips.text: For smart stripe-on-stripe outfits, use shades of one colour, such as tonal navy, rather than stark black and white.
tips.why: Tonal stripes look refined; black and white stripes look costume-like.
sources: An Expert Guide To Pattern Mixing

tips.text: Pair houndstooth only with simple patterns such as a narrow pinstripe or large polka dots.
tips.why: Houndstooth is already busy and fights other complex prints.
sources: An Expert Guide To Pattern Mixing

tips.text: Tame a paisley piece by repeating one of its colours elsewhere in the outfit.
tips.why: The repeated colour ties an intense print to the rest of the look.
sources: An Expert Guide To Pattern Mixing

tips.text: Wear polka dots mainly on accessories such as ties, pocket squares and socks, set against straight-line patterns like stripes or checks.
tips.why: Dots are easiest in small doses and contrast well with lines.
sources: An Expert Guide To Pattern Mixing

tips.text: With a check suit, try a striped tie and a polka-dot pocket square in a sober palette.
tips.why: Three different pattern types in quiet colours mix without clashing.
sources: An Expert Guide To Pattern Mixing

tips.text: Choose the shirt first, then a tie that picks up one of the colours in it.
tips.why: A shared colour makes the two look coordinated.
sources: How To Match Your Shirt And Tie

tips.text: When both shirt and tie are patterned, make the tie's pattern the larger, bolder one.
tips.why: The tie should lead and the shirt sit behind it.
sources: How To Match Your Shirt And Tie

tips.text: Match tie and shirt texture to the setting: smooth silk and sleek shirting for business, coarser textured fabrics for relaxed occasions.
tips.why: Shine reads formal; texture reads casual.
sources: How To Match Your Shirt And Tie

tips.text: Own a knitted tie; it dresses up with a suit or down with chinos and a cardigan.
tips.why: It covers uncertain dress codes such as some interviews.
sources: How To Match Your Shirt And Tie

tips.text: If you are slim, avoid oversized collars and very wide lapels.
tips.why: Big details overwhelm a slight frame.
sources: How To Match Your Shirt And Tie

tips.text: If you are stocky, avoid skinny ties and narrow collars.
tips.why: Small details make a broad frame look bigger by contrast.
sources: How To Match Your Shirt And Tie

tips.text: A thick or heavy tie needs a deeper, larger shirt collar.
tips.why: A bulky knot crowds a small collar.
sources: How To Match Your Shirt And Tie

tips.text: Tie a firm, neat knot and pinch a small dimple below it.
tips.why: A loose knot looks sloppy; the dimple adds polish.
sources: How To Match Your Shirt And Tie

tips.text: If you're short, have one pair of trousers hemmed to the perfect length and use it as the template for hemming every future pair.
tips.why: Off-the-rack trousers are usually too long and pool at the ankle.
sources: Essential Fashion Tips For Short Men

tips.text: Wear trousers sitting a couple of inches below the navel and tuck in your shirt or knit.
tips.why: A higher waistline makes the legs look longer.
sources: Essential Fashion Tips For Short Men

tips.text: Short men should choose slim or tapered cuts over baggy or boxy ones.
tips.why: Excess fabric swamps a small frame and makes it look smaller.
sources: Essential Fashion Tips For Short Men

tips.text: Keep trousers plain and neutral and put pattern and detail on your top half.
tips.why: Detail near the face draws the eye upward; loud trousers pull it down.
sources: Essential Fashion Tips For Short Men

tips.text: Short men suit a slim suit with narrow lapels and the jacket button placed slightly above the navel.
tips.why: One column of colour and a high button point lengthen the body.
sources: Essential Fashion Tips For Short Men

tips.text: Choose shirts that end around the hips rather than long, boxy ones.
tips.why: A shorter hem shows more leg; boxy cuts look dumpy.
sources: Essential Fashion Tips For Short Men

tips.text: Favour cropped jackets such as a Harrington or bomber, and keep overcoats above mid-thigh.
tips.why: Long coats swamp a short frame like a cape.
sources: Essential Fashion Tips For Short Men

tips.text: Build your pocket squares from plain colours first, starting with white, before adding patterns.
tips.why: Plain squares go with almost any jacket and tie.
sources: The Complete Guide To Men's Pocket Squares

tips.text: Choose patterned squares in classic motifs such as paisley, dots or checks, in jewel tones or neutrals.
tips.why: Timeless patterns and colours combine with more outfits.
sources: The Complete Guide To Men's Pocket Squares

tips.text: Keep pocket squares clean and wash them when they look grubby.
tips.why: A soiled square undoes a polished outfit.
sources: The Complete Guide To Men's Pocket Squares

tips.text: Look for pocket squares with hand-rolled edges rather than flat machine hems.
tips.why: Rolled edges show better craftsmanship and sit better in the pocket.
sources: The Complete Guide To Men's Pocket Squares

tips.text: Carry a separate handkerchief in another pocket for actual use; the pocket square is for show.
tips.why: It keeps the square clean and presentable.
sources: The Complete Guide To Men's Pocket Squares

tips.text: Use crisp cotton or linen for sharp straight or one-point folds, and silk for soft puff or two-point folds.
tips.why: Each fabric holds a different kind of shape.
sources: The Complete Guide To Men's Pocket Squares

tips.text: Use small, neat folds with small patterns such as gingham.
tips.why: A small fold shows little fabric, so a large pattern gets lost.
sources: The Complete Guide To Men's Pocket Squares

tips.text: For business or formal outfits, use a white or light blue cotton square in a straight or one-point fold.
tips.why: It looks crisp and sober.
sources: The Complete Guide To Men's Pocket Squares

tips.text: With a dinner jacket and bow tie, wear a simple square fold.
tips.why: A clean straight line suits black tie.
sources: The Complete Guide To Men's Pocket Squares

tips.text: Save a casual silk puff fold for smart separates rather than a business suit.
tips.why: The relaxed puff clashes with strict business tailoring.
sources: The Complete Guide To Men's Pocket Squares

tips.text: Don't wear socks with strappy sandals.
tips.why: Most people still see it as a style mistake.
sources: Men's Socks: What To Wear And When

tips.text: With shorts, wear no-show socks unless you want a deliberately sporty, skate look with crew socks.
tips.why: Visible socks with shorts look dated unless the look is sporty on purpose.
sources: Men's Socks: What To Wear And When

tips.text: In winter, wear thin patterned socks with loafers.
tips.why: They add warmth and a little interest at the ankle.
sources: Men's Socks: What To Wear And When

tips.text: With boots, wear thicker mid-calf ribbed socks with some wool in them.
tips.why: Stiff boots rub the ankle without the extra padding.
sources: Men's Socks: What To Wear And When

tips.text: Socks don't have to match exactly; a harmonious contrast works, and navy or dark grey is the safe default.
tips.why: Dark neutral socks go with almost any trouser and shoe.
sources: Men's Socks: What To Wear And When

tips.text: Don't match your socks to your tie.
tips.why: It looks affected and over-planned.
sources: Men's Socks: What To Wear And When

tips.text: Keep patterned socks for casual outfits and echo one of their colours elsewhere in the look.
tips.why: The repeated colour ties the pattern into the outfit.
sources: Men's Socks: What To Wear And When

tips.text: Choose ribbed socks in cooler weather.
tips.why: The ribbing grips the leg so the sock stays up, and adds warmth.
sources: Men's Socks: What To Wear And When

tips.text: Cut an overcoat slightly generous through the shoulders and waist so a tailored jacket fits underneath without being squashed.
tips.why: A tight coat creases the jacket beneath it and can damage its shoulders.
sources: How an overcoat should fit: Cifonelli fitting

tips.text: Try an overcoat on over the jacket you'll wear with it: it should slip on and off easily and never pinch the shoulders.
tips.why: Feeling squashed means the coat is too small for its main job.
sources: How an overcoat should fit: Cifonelli fitting

tips.text: Keep shoulder padding in an overcoat to a minimum.
tips.why: The jacket underneath already gives structure, so extra padding just stacks up and looks bulky.
sources: How an overcoat should fit: Cifonelli fitting

tips.text: Choose a soft, shirt-style shoulder on a coat you'll mostly wear over knitwear.
tips.why: It reads more casual and sits more naturally over a sweater than a built-up shoulder.
sources: How an overcoat should fit: Cifonelli fitting

tips.text: Pick a coat with a belt or adjustable waist if you'll often wear it over just a knit.
tips.why: Cinching it takes out the extra room meant for a jacket so it doesn't look baggy.
sources: How an overcoat should fit: Cifonelli fitting

tips.text: Line an overcoat in silk or a slippery synthetic rather than cashmere; get warmth from a heavier outer cloth instead.
tips.why: A smooth lining slides over jacket sleeves, while a fuzzy one catches.
sources: How an overcoat should fit: Cifonelli fitting

tips.text: Make sure the overcoat collar stands high enough at the back to cover your shirt collar.
tips.why: Otherwise rain runs onto the shirt collar.
sources: How an overcoat should fit: Cifonelli fitting

tips.text: A second-hand coat a couple of inches too big in the chest can usually be taken in, and a belt hides leftover looseness.
tips.why: Good vintage coats are worth adjusting rather than passing over.
sources: How an overcoat should fit: Cifonelli fitting

tips.text: Belt and shoes needn't be the exact same shade, but keep them closely related, such as a mid-brown belt with dark brown shoes.
tips.why: Browns from one family sit together without looking forced.
sources: Should your belt match your shoes? (Or bag)

tips.text: A brown belt can go with brown suede shoes even if the shades differ slightly.
tips.why: Suede and leather browns are close relatives.
sources: Should your belt match your shoes? (Or bag)

tips.text: Canvas webbing belts and fabric NATO watch straps don't need to match your shoes.
tips.why: Non-leather pieces escape the leather-matching rules.
sources: Should your belt match your shoes? (Or bag)

tips.text: If you mostly wear suits with black shoes, carry a black briefcase; for casual versatility, choose dark brown.
tips.why: Black is the most elegant with formal wear; dark brown spans more outfits.
sources: Should your belt match your shoes? (Or bag)

tips.text: Match the bag's formality to the outfit: attaché case most formal, then briefcase, then tote.
tips.why: A casual bag undermines a sharp suit, and vice versa.
sources: Should your belt match your shoes? (Or bag)

tips.text: Choose linen for hot-weather shirts, and use it to try brighter colours.
tips.why: Its open weave breathes, and the texture softens strong colours so they're easier to wear.
sources: How to Dress Well in Summer

tips.text: Avoid linen head to toe; mix it with other summer cloths such as wool fresco, seersucker, madras or silk.
tips.why: An all-linen outfit looks too crumpled.
sources: How to Dress Well in Summer

tips.text: Pair a relaxed, crumpled linen shirt with sharply pressed trousers.
tips.why: The contrast between rumpled and crisp textures looks deliberate.
sources: How to Dress Well in Summer

tips.text: When buying an unstructured summer jacket, judge the cut: without padding or canvas, only good tailoring keeps it in shape.
tips.why: Soft jackets are harder to make well, not cheaper.
sources: How to Dress Well in Summer

tips.text: For a summer cocktail dress code, a dark suit is enough; a dinner jacket with cream or ecru trousers is the more striking choice.
tips.why: Cocktail dress leans towards evening wear.
sources: How to Dress Well in Summer

tips.text: In hot weather, avoid swinging between stiff formality and sloppy casual; light tailored cloths keep you cool and well dressed.
tips.why: Summer dressing goes wrong at both extremes.
sources: How to Dress Well in Summer

tips.text: Keep seasonal cloths such as flannel and tweed for autumn and winter instead of wearing year-round worsted suits all the time.
tips.why: Seasonal fabrics are warmer and have more texture and character.
sources: What to Wear in Autumn

tips.text: Use tweed to bring colour into a conservative wardrobe.
tips.why: Its mixed yarns carry colour and pattern without looking loud.
sources: What to Wear in Autumn

tips.text: For houndstooth or glen check, consider flannel cloth.
tips.why: Flannel's soft surface blends the contrasting shades, so the check looks gentler.
sources: What to Wear in Autumn

tips.text: Own grey flannel trousers: they go with jackets of any colour or texture and look more elegant than jeans.
tips.why: They are the most versatile odd trouser for cold months.
sources: What to Wear in Autumn

tips.text: Dress down a flannel suit by swapping shirt and tie for a cashmere roll-neck and suede shoes.
tips.why: It stays elegant while feeling relaxed and smart casual.
sources: What to Wear in Autumn

tips.text: Wear a tweed hacking jacket off duty with a roll-neck, slim wool trousers, Chelsea boots and a knotted scarf.
tips.why: It makes a country jacket look modern and easy.
sources: What to Wear in Autumn

tips.text: Pair a Norfolk or heavy tweed jacket with dark jeans and suede chukkas or loafers, not cavalry twills and a flat cap, when in town.
tips.why: Full country dress in the city looks like a costume.
sources: What to Wear in Autumn

tips.text: Choose woollen flannel for warmth and rustic character, worsted flannel for a lighter, sharper business suit.
tips.why: Woollen yarn is thicker and fuzzier; worsted is finer and smoother.
sources: What to Wear in Autumn

tips.text: Give each layer a different fabric or texture.
tips.why: Varied surfaces add depth, and each piece can change role as the weather shifts.
sources: How To Get Your Layers Right

tips.text: Build autumn layers so the outfit still works when one is taken off, e.g. tee, cardigan, suede jacket and coat over jeans.
tips.why: Temperatures change through the day, and you'll shed layers.
sources: How To Get Your Layers Right

tips.text: Layer tonally within one colour family, such as browns or blues, then add one piece in a contrasting shade.
tips.why: Tonal looks are balanced, and the contrast stops them looking flat.
sources: How To Get Your Layers Right

tips.text: Repeat small details or colours across layers to tie an outfit together.
tips.why: Echoes make several pieces read as one deliberate look.
sources: How To Get Your Layers Right

tips.text: Contrast glossy shoes, such as polished leather loafers, with matte or textured clothes.
tips.why: The shine adds polish against soft fabrics.
sources: How To Get Your Layers Right

tips.text: Add pattern in a top layer, such as a sweater vest over a shirt or a striped long-sleeved tee.
tips.why: It brings interest without changing the whole outfit.
sources: How To Get Your Layers Right

tips.text: Use a plain cable-knit over a bolder piece to calm it down.
tips.why: The solid knit grounds the louder layer beneath.
sources: How To Get Your Layers Right

tips.text: Put a bold colour in a base or middle layer, soften it with neutral outer layers, and echo it in socks or sneaker details.
tips.why: The colour shows without overwhelming the outfit.
sources: How To Get Your Layers Right

tips.text: Build a streetwear look on three essentials: a sweatshirt, sneakers and a cap.
tips.why: These pieces carry the style.
sources: Tips: How to dress in a STREETWEAR style?

tips.text: Choose sweatshirts and hoodies in plain colours rather than loud prints.
tips.why: Plain pieces combine more easily and look less juvenile.
sources: Tips: How to dress in a STREETWEAR style?

tips.text: Wear a zip hoodie either open over a good T-shirt or zipped up fully.
tips.why: Both look intentional; the tee becomes part of the outfit when it is open.
sources: Tips: How to dress in a STREETWEAR style?

tips.text: Check a crew-neck sweatshirt's fit: neckline at the start of the shoulders, ribbing neither tight nor long, and shape recovering after you raise your arms.
tips.why: Poorly made sweatshirts lose their shape fast.
sources: Tips: How to dress in a STREETWEAR style?

tips.text: Layer a buttoned shirt under a crew-neck sweatshirt, ideally one with interesting fabric details.
tips.why: It adds a smarter, more considered note.
sources: Tips: How to dress in a STREETWEAR style?

tips.text: Pick simple, versatile sneakers and avoid flashy colours or bulky oversized shapes.
tips.why: Sneakers should blend into the outfit, not steal attention.
sources: Tips: How to dress in a STREETWEAR style?

tips.text: Choose a well-sized cap in a classic colour with a discreet logo.
tips.why: Loud or ill-fitting caps cheapen the look.
sources: Tips: How to dress in a STREETWEAR style?

tips.text: Avoid caps with a white inner sweatband.
tips.why: It shows sweat marks quickly.
sources: Tips: How to dress in a STREETWEAR style?

tips.text: Use fine stripes or heathered cotton to add interest to plain tops instead of graphics.
tips.why: They give texture without shouting.
sources: Tips: How to dress in a STREETWEAR style?

tips.text: With brightly coloured chinos, keep the rest of the outfit neutral.
tips.why: One strong colour is enough.
sources: Tips: How to dress in a STREETWEAR style?

tips.text: Shorts should end around the knee, without bulky extra pockets.
tips.why: That length and a clean leg look neater.
sources: Tips: How to dress in a STREETWEAR style?

tips.text: Lift a streetwear outfit with one premium piece such as a chunky knit, a poplin shirt or a quilted jacket.
tips.why: The contrast makes the look more grown-up.
sources: Tips: How to dress in a STREETWEAR style?

tips.text: When a hoodie goes with tailored pieces, pick one with little or no logo.
tips.why: Loud branding fights with sharper clothes.
sources: You Asked: How Do I Make Streetwear Smart?

tips.text: Choose a mid-weight hoodie to layer under a jacket.
tips.why: A thick one bunches up and looks bulky beneath tailoring.
sources: You Asked: How Do I Make Streetwear Smart?

tips.text: Look to streetwear labels' more refined pieces, such as work jackets, and wear them over a collared shirt.
tips.why: They bridge street style and smart dressing.
sources: You Asked: How Do I Make Streetwear Smart?

tips.text: Swap jeans for tailored trousers, ideally navy, to sharpen a streetwear outfit.
tips.why: Trousers lift the formality while the rest stays relaxed.
sources: You Asked: How Do I Make Streetwear Smart?

tips.text: To smarten streetwear, choose minimal low-profile sneakers over chunky trainers.
tips.why: Bulky trainers pull attention away from the rest of the outfit.
sources: You Asked: How Do I Make Streetwear Smart?

tips.text: Plan how street and smart pieces combine instead of throwing them together at random.
tips.why: The mix only works when it looks deliberate.
sources: You Asked: How Do I Make Streetwear Smart?

tips.text: Aim for a moderate fit, neither very slim nor very baggy.
tips.why: Both extremes are common mistakes; a middle fit is a safe baseline.
sources: A Practical Guide To Getting Started

tips.text: Test fit while moving: a shirt shouldn't strain when you sit, and a jacket should let you lift your arms.
tips.why: Clothes have to work in motion, not just standing in a mirror.
sources: A Practical Guide To Getting Started

tips.text: Clear out clothes that are worn out, dated or never suited you, and sell or donate them.
tips.why: A smaller wardrobe of things you'll wear is easier to dress from.
sources: A Practical Guide To Getting Started

tips.text: Shop for the life you actually lead and what you wear most, not trends or a lifestyle you don't have.
tips.why: Clothes that suit your habits get worn; the rest sits unused.
sources: A Practical Guide To Getting Started

tips.text: While you're still learning, buy mid-priced pieces and treat early purchases as experiments.
tips.why: Your taste will change and you'll likely replace them.
sources: A Practical Guide To Getting Started

tips.text: Look at second-hand and thrift shops, locally or online, for well-made clothes.
tips.why: Good pieces can be found for much less.
sources: A Practical Guide To Getting Started

tips.text: Never buy something just because it's on sale.
tips.why: A discount doesn't make an unneeded or ill-fitting piece useful.
sources: A Practical Guide To Getting Started

tips.text: Train your eye by studying outfits you admire: where seams fall, how cloth drapes and where garments end.
tips.why: Recognising good fit and proportion takes years of looking.
sources: A Practical Guide To Getting Started

tips.text: Have your feet measured properly before buying good shoes.
tips.why: Many men wear the wrong shoe size.
sources: A Practical Guide To Getting Started

tips.text: When an invitation names a dress code, follow it; when it says nothing, smart casual is a safe default.
tips.why: It suits most gatherings without looking out of place.
sources: Esquire's Complete and Comprehensive Guide to Smart-Casual Style

tips.text: Keep black-tie pieces such as patent tuxedo shoes out of smart-casual outfits.
tips.why: Evening-formal items look strange next to workwear trousers and other casual pieces.
sources: Esquire's Complete and Comprehensive Guide to Smart-Casual Style

tips.text: Alternate smart and casual pieces from top to bottom, for example a smart shirt, relaxed trousers and smart shoes.
tips.why: The swap keeps the outfit balanced between dressy and easy.
sources: Esquire's Complete and Comprehensive Guide to Smart-Casual Style

tips.text: When layering a smart-casual look, make one layer smart and the other casual, like a plain tee under a tailored blazer.
tips.why: Mixing levels in the layers gives the relaxed-but-polished balance.
sources: Esquire's Complete and Comprehensive Guide to Smart-Casual Style

tips.text: Keep a smart-casual outfit simple rather than piling on many pieces.
tips.why: Too many elements look messy instead of sharp.
sources: Esquire's Complete and Comprehensive Guide to Smart-Casual Style

tips.text: Put money into timeless staples such as a wool coat and good leather shoes rather than passing trends.
tips.why: They last longer and never go out of date.
sources: Esquire's Complete and Comprehensive Guide to Smart-Casual Style

tips.text: For smart casual, pick a soft, unstructured blazer over a stiff, formal one.
tips.why: A rigid blazer looks like office tailoring and fights the relaxed pieces.
sources: Esquire's Complete and Comprehensive Guide to Smart-Casual Style

tips.text: Use shoes to tune the formality: loafers lift a casual outfit, sneakers relax a dressier one.
tips.why: Footwear shifts the whole look up or down quickly.
sources: Esquire's Complete and Comprehensive Guide to Smart-Casual Style

tips.text: Wear a button-down shirt in different ways: fully buttoned, open over a tee, or layered under a jacket or coat.
tips.why: One shirt then covers several levels of formality.
sources: Esquire's Complete and Comprehensive Guide to Smart-Casual Style

tips.text: A plain white tee works on its own or under a denim jacket or blazer.
tips.why: It is the most adaptable base layer.
sources: Esquire's Complete and Comprehensive Guide to Smart-Casual Style

tips.text: Match the room: cargo trousers at a gathering where everyone else wears smart trousers will look out of place.
tips.why: Smart casual still has to fit the setting.
sources: Esquire's Complete and Comprehensive Guide to Smart-Casual Style

tips.text: For a business-casual office, choose jeans that are slim but not skinny, mostly in a dark wash such as raw indigo or black.
tips.why: Dark, neat denim is the smartest version of jeans.
sources: How to dress for business casual at the office

tips.text: Balance office jeans with a crisp oxford shirt or a blazer.
tips.why: It stops the outfit sliding into weekend casual.
sources: How to dress for business casual at the office

tips.text: Light-wash jeans can work at the office only if they are slim and rip-free; dress them up with a white oxford and a navy or khaki blazer.
tips.why: A light wash already reads casual, so the rest must be sharper.
sources: How to dress for business casual at the office

tips.text: With light-wash jeans at work, wear loafers or Chelsea boots rather than sneakers.
tips.why: Sneakers would push an already casual wash too far.
sources: How to dress for business casual at the office

tips.text: Office sneakers should be minimal and streamlined; keep bold, loud pairs for off-duty hours.
tips.why: Plain sneakers blend with tailoring, statement pairs don't.
sources: How to dress for business casual at the office

tips.text: Rely on oxford shirts to keep business casual buttoned-up; white is the safest colour, alone or under a blazer.
tips.why: A collared oxford holds the outfit above casual.
sources: How to dress for business casual at the office

tips.text: Make a navy blazer, structured or unstructured, the staple of a business-casual wardrobe.
tips.why: It goes with almost every office outfit.
sources: How to dress for business casual at the office

tips.text: In a business-casual workplace, save the full suit for board meetings and job interviews.
tips.why: A suit every day looks overdressed in a relaxed office.
sources: How to dress for business casual at the office

tips.text: Skip technical mountain or sports jackets at the office; a trench or mac covers cool, wet days.
tips.why: Performance outerwear looks out of place over office clothes.
sources: How to dress for business casual at the office

tips.text: Patent oxfords are the classic black-tie shoe, but plain, highly polished black calf oxfords are acceptable and easier to wear again.
tips.why: Both keep the shoe sleek and plain.
sources: Black Tie Dress Code: A Modern Man's Guide For 2026

tips.text: With a dinner suit, choose a turn-down collar shirt over a wing collar; a pleated or bib front is optional.
tips.why: Wing collars belong with white tie and look dated with a dinner suit.
sources: Black Tie Dress Code: A Modern Man's Guide For 2026

tips.text: Tie your own bow tie instead of wearing a clip-on or pre-tied one.
tips.why: Pre-tied bows look like costume.
sources: Black Tie Dress Code: A Modern Man's Guide For 2026

tips.text: If you wear a cummerbund, make it black; coloured ones, especially red, look dated.
tips.why: Black keeps the outfit uniform.
sources: Black Tie Dress Code: A Modern Man's Guide For 2026

tips.text: Avoid trendy cuts such as very skinny lapels or cropped trousers on a dinner suit.
tips.why: You will wear it for years, and fashion details date fast.
sources: Black Tie Dress Code: A Modern Man's Guide For 2026

tips.text: Keep black-tie accessories minimal: a slim dress watch in the same metal as your cufflinks and a simply folded white pocket square.
tips.why: Restraint looks elegant in a formal uniform.
sources: Black Tie Dress Code: A Modern Man's Guide For 2026

tips.text: Own and tailor your dinner suit rather than renting, with moderate lapels and precisely hemmed trousers.
tips.why: Ill-fitting polyester rental suits undermine the whole look.
sources: Black Tie Dress Code: A Modern Man's Guide For 2026

tips.text: Break black-tie rules only when the invitation allows it; a roll neck or black tee instead of shirt and bow tie suits 'eveningwear' invitations only.
tips.why: Creative swaps at a strict black-tie event look disrespectful.
sources: Black Tie Dress Code: A Modern Man's Guide For 2026

tips.text: When a holiday party's dress code is unclear, lean towards the formal end, unless the hosts have said it's a playful ugly-sweater party.
tips.why: Nobody faults a guest for looking put together.
sources: Holiday Attire for Men: What It Means & How to Wear It

tips.text: If you're unsure what a holiday invitation expects, ask the hosts directly.
tips.why: Following their dress code is a courtesy.
sources: Holiday Attire for Men: What It Means & How to Wear It

tips.text: Read 'holiday attire' as cocktail attire with a festive touch, such as tartan or a seasonal colour.
tips.why: It keeps the formality while marking the season.
sources: Holiday Attire for Men: What It Means & How to Wear It

tips.text: Use festive reds and greens in muted, deep shades rather than bright ones.
tips.why: Bright seasonal colours quickly look clownish.
sources: Holiday Attire for Men: What It Means & How to Wear It

tips.text: For an office holiday party, wear your normal work outfit, slightly relaxed and with one seasonal touch.
tips.why: It stays appropriate in front of colleagues while feeling festive.
sources: Holiday Attire for Men: What It Means & How to Wear It

tips.text: With conservative holiday tailoring, wear black cap-toe oxfords or dark brown or oxblood shoes, not light tan.
tips.why: Light tan is too casual for a dark suit.
sources: Holiday Attire for Men: What It Means & How to Wear It

tips.text: Skip novelty ties with Santa or similar motifs; choose a dark burgundy or muted tie, plain or subtly patterned.
tips.why: Novelty prints look juvenile with tailoring.
sources: Holiday Attire for Men: What It Means & How to Wear It

tips.text: Keep cufflinks, tie bars and rings understated and in matching metals.
tips.why: Coordinated, quiet jewellery looks refined.
sources: Holiday Attire for Men: What It Means & How to Wear It

tips.text: In a less formal office, a textured or patterned sport coat (herringbone, houndstooth, tweed or tartan) with flannel or corduroy trousers suits a winter party.
tips.why: Rustic textures feel seasonal while staying smart.
sources: Holiday Attire for Men: What It Means & How to Wear It

tips.text: For casual offices and house parties, wear a cardigan, cable knit or Fair Isle sweater in warm colours with dark denim or coloured chinos.
tips.why: Cosy knits look festive without needing a suit.
sources: Holiday Attire for Men: What It Means & How to Wear It

tips.text: Dress at least business casual for an interview, even at a casual employer; never turn up in weekend clothes.
tips.why: Few interviewers mind a smarter look, many mind a sloppy one.
sources: 10 Things Men Should NEVER Wear to a Job Interview

tips.text: Wear a collared button-up shirt to an interview, even for a hands-on job.
tips.why: It signals respect, not that you'd dress that way on the job.
sources: 10 Things Men Should NEVER Wear to a Job Interview

tips.text: Wear new interview clothes a few times beforehand and leave two to three weeks for alterations.
tips.why: Comfortable, well-fitting clothes help you feel confident.
sources: 10 Things Men Should NEVER Wear to a Job Interview

tips.text: Remove labels, pins and tacking stitches from new clothes and smooth out packaging creases before wearing them.
tips.why: Leftover tags make you look inattentive.
sources: 10 Things Men Should NEVER Wear to a Job Interview

tips.text: Wear dress trousers or chinos to an interview, not shorts, cargos or sweatpants; if you must wear jeans, add a blazer or sport coat.
tips.why: Jeans still read casual on their own.
sources: 10 Things Men Should NEVER Wear to a Job Interview

tips.text: Skip logos, slogans, flashy jewellery, bold prints and loud colours when interviewing.
tips.why: The interviewer should focus on you, not your clothes.
sources: 10 Things Men Should NEVER Wear to a Job Interview

tips.text: Take out earbuds and silence or remove beeping smartwatches before the interview.
tips.why: Visible or noisy tech looks inattentive and distracts.
sources: 10 Things Men Should NEVER Wear to a Job Interview

tips.text: Avoid an all-black suit, shirt and tie combination at a wedding.
tips.why: The monochrome look is dated and grabs attention.
sources: What to Wear as a Wedding Guest

tips.text: Leave top hats, ascots, gloves and showy boutonnieres to the wedding party unless you're asked to wear them.
tips.why: Those pieces signal a special role in the ceremony.
sources: What to Wear as a Wedding Guest

tips.text: Start planning a wedding-guest outfit at least a month before the date.
tips.why: It leaves time to find pieces and get alterations done.
sources: What to Wear as a Wedding Guest

tips.text: If ceremony and reception have different dress codes and there's no time to change, dress for the more formal one.
tips.why: Being slightly overdressed at the party beats being underdressed at the ceremony.
sources: What to Wear as a Wedding Guest

tips.text: Daytime, warm-weather and outdoor weddings allow lighter, more relaxed clothes; weddings in places of worship call for more formality.
tips.why: Time, season and venue shift how formal the day is.
sources: What to Wear as a Wedding Guest

tips.text: Navy and charcoal suits are the most versatile wedding-guest choices, in lighter or heavier wool depending on the season.
tips.why: Sober dark colours fit almost any dress code.
sources: What to Wear as a Wedding Guest

tips.text: At a wedding, wear dark brown oxfords or derbies by day and black ones in the evening.
tips.why: Black reads more formal and suits evening events.
sources: What to Wear as a Wedding Guest

tips.text: A necktie suits most wedding dress codes; save bow ties for formal evening events.
tips.why: A bow tie with a day suit can look whimsical.
sources: What to Wear as a Wedding Guest

tips.text: For a cocktail-attire wedding, wear a dark grey or navy suit with a white or light blue shirt, or dark brown for an outdoor daytime event.
tips.why: Dark suits meet the code without straying into black tie.
sources: What to Wear as a Wedding Guest

tips.text: For black tie optional, a plain dark grey or dark blue suit with a white shirt and black plain-toe oxfords is the right alternative to a tuxedo.
tips.why: It matches the formality without a dinner suit.
sources: What to Wear as a Wedding Guest

tips.text: Add personality with a pocket square and a small boutonniere in a harmonising colour, balanced so neither overpowers the other.
tips.why: Small accents show care without stealing attention.
sources: What to Wear as a Wedding Guest

tips.text: The more formal the wedding, the more restrained your accessories should be.
tips.why: Formal dress codes leave less room for flourishes.
sources: What to Wear as a Wedding Guest

tips.text: For outdoor summer weddings, linen or seersucker suits are good choices.
tips.why: They keep you cool and suit warm daytime settings.
sources: What to Wear as a Wedding Guest

tips.text: Plan your outfits ahead for a busy summer social calendar.
tips.why: Packed weeks of events are easy when the right clothes are ready.
sources: How To Crack Every Summer Party Dress Code

tips.text: At a hot destination wedding, choose light, flowing fabrics and easy layers over a heavy suit.
tips.why: Heat and several outfit changes make heavy tailoring impractical.
sources: How To Crack Every Summer Party Dress Code

tips.text: Cut summer trousers wide enough to let air through and long enough to rest on the shoe.
tips.why: Roomy legs keep you cool and the full length keeps them smart.
sources: How To Crack Every Summer Party Dress Code

tips.text: Bring colour to a wedding outfit through a patterned tie or a bright pocket square.
tips.why: Accessories add personality without overwhelming the tailoring.
sources: How To Crack Every Summer Party Dress Code

tips.text: At summer spectator sport such as tennis, racing or cricket, wear a light unstructured beige blazer, livened up with a colourful shirt or club tie.
tips.why: A pale, light jacket handles heat and suits the daytime setting.
sources: How To Crack Every Summer Party Dress Code

tips.text: At a summer work party, skip the tie unless one is requested and avoid stiff collars.
tips.why: The event should feel relaxed, not like another day at the desk.
sources: How To Crack Every Summer Party Dress Code

tips.text: At a summer work party, wear a blazer only if it is very informal, and choose a low-key shirt over a vest or tank top.
tips.why: Relaxed but never showy or too bare in front of colleagues.
sources: How To Crack Every Summer Party Dress Code

tips.text: At a wedding in a hot country, keep the tie but switch to a linen suit, and add a hat rather than resort to flip-flops.
tips.why: You stay smart while respecting the climate.
sources: The Wedding Style Guide: It's not about you

tips.text: Choose a wedding suit that looks less like business wear, such as light grey or double-breasted.
tips.why: It marks the day as a special occasion.
sources: The Wedding Style Guide: It's not about you

tips.text: A navy suit looks less like office wear when it is double-breasted or in a textured cloth such as herringbone.
tips.why: Cut and texture take it away from the business uniform.
sources: The Wedding Style Guide: It's not about you

tips.text: Put a wedding outfit's colour into the pocket square and buttonhole rather than the tie or socks.
tips.why: Small accents add cheer while the core stays elegant.
sources: The Wedding Style Guide: It's not about you

tips.text: Gauge a wedding's formality from the invitation, what you know of the hosts, or someone close to them; if in doubt, dress smartly.
tips.why: It's the hosts' event, and their expectations set the level.
sources: The Wedding Style Guide: It's not about you

tips.text: Follow a wedding's dress code even when it's unusual, such as black tie in the daytime or beachwear.
tips.why: Respecting the hosts' wishes matters more than convention.
sources: The Wedding Style Guide: It's not about you

tips.text: Judge a shoe's formality by shape and decoration as well as colour: a sleek chocolate oxford can be dressier than a plain black derby.
tips.why: Broguing and chunky shapes relax a shoe; sleek closed lacing dresses it up.
sources: How To Match Clothes and Shoes For Guys: Outfit Color Guide

tips.text: Treat trainers by their own rules: white trainers suit nearly everything, while white dress shoes look odd.
tips.why: Sneaker conventions differ from those of leather dress shoes.
sources: How To Match Clothes and Shoes For Guys: Outfit Color Guide

tips.text: Let bright or colourful shoes be the loudest thing you wear, keeping the rest of the outfit neutral.
tips.why: Several strong colours compete and look messy.
sources: How To Match Clothes and Shoes For Guys: Outfit Color Guide

tips.text: With jeans, choose black derbies or Chelsea boots rather than black oxfords.
tips.why: Oxfords are too dressy for denim and casual trousers.
sources: How To Match Clothes and Shoes For Guys: Outfit Color Guide

tips.text: Don't wear black leather shoes with shorts.
tips.why: The combination looks like a school uniform.
sources: How To Match Clothes and Shoes For Guys: Outfit Color Guide

tips.text: Keep brown shoes a couple of shades away from brown trousers instead of matching them closely.
tips.why: A near-match looks accidental; a clear contrast looks intended.
sources: How To Match Clothes and Shoes For Guys: Outfit Color Guide

tips.text: Treat tan as the most casual brown: best in brogues, boots and suede with jeans and chinos.
tips.why: Light brown reads relaxed and lightens an outfit.
sources: How To Match Clothes and Shoes For Guys: Outfit Color Guide

tips.text: With shorts, wear laceless or suede shoes such as loafers rather than lace-up leather.
tips.why: They match the relaxed feel of shorts.
sources: How To Match Clothes and Shoes For Guys: Outfit Color Guide

tips.text: Keep white trainers spotless with protective spray and wipes, and never wear battered trainers with tailoring.
tips.why: Their appeal depends on looking clean.
sources: How To Match Clothes and Shoes For Guys: Outfit Color Guide

tips.text: Dressing down still takes effort; choose casual clothes you feel genuinely comfortable in.
tips.why: Discomfort shows and makes the outfit look careless or forced.
sources: You Asked: How Do You Wear Double Denim?

tips.text: Move toward casual clothes step by step from your comfort zone, not in one sudden jump.
tips.why: An abrupt switch, like monk straps straight to sneakers, looks borrowed.
sources: You Asked: How Do You Wear Double Denim?

tips.text: To ease away from suits, start with chinos and a shirt with the sleeves rolled up.
tips.why: It is a gentle first step toward relaxed dressing.
sources: You Asked: How Do You Wear Double Denim?

tips.text: Choose trouser width for your frame: wide legs can swamp a very slim man, while tight tapers make sitting uncomfortable.
tips.why: Proportion and practicality matter more than the trend.
sources: You Asked: How Do You Wear Double Denim?

tips.text: For double denim, stick to classic blue shades and skip novelty colours.
tips.why: Odd colours turn it into a loud statement.
sources: You Asked: How Do You Wear Double Denim?

tips.text: Wear different denim shades top and bottom, such as a darker jacket over lighter jeans.
tips.why: The contrast keeps it from looking like a matching uniform.
sources: You Asked: How Do You Wear Double Denim?

tips.text: Keep double denim simple with a striped Breton T-shirt and clean white sneakers.
tips.why: Plain classics let the denim do the work.
sources: You Asked: How Do You Wear Double Denim?

tips.text: Have your key suits and jackets made to measure, choosing the cloth and details yourself.
tips.why: Tailoring cut to your body makes a visible difference.
sources: How To Dress Like An Italian

tips.text: Wear blue tonally, but don't pair a jacket and trousers in two different blues for formal wear.
tips.why: Two near-matching blues look like a mistake rather than a choice.
sources: How To Dress Like An Italian

tips.text: Treat neutrals as more than beige and camel; wear brighter, lighter neutrals in summer.
